+Align

Category / Categoría: Herramientas y software

Definition (EN)

Tool for aligning existing corpora in two languages to create parallel corpora.

Definición (ES)

Herramienta para alinear corpus existentes en dos lenguas y crear así corpus paralelos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • alignment — +Align performs alignment.
  • LF Aligner — LF Aligner is another aligner.
  • parallel corpus — It is used to build parallel corpora.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • Term not attested in the English subcorpus.

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • Afortunadamente ya existen varias herramientas que ayudan a la confección de corpus paralelos (Sketch Engine, PENCIL) o que sirven para alinear corpus existentes que estén en dos lenguas distintas (como LF Aligner, Bitext2tmx o +Align). 6. (2023_Lázaro, J._Los corpus como fuente de datos lexicográficos)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

Entry written by Claude from corpus contexts.

accuracy

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A measure of the correctness of data annotation, defined as the proportion of true positive results among all instances identified by a query. This term is crucial in evaluating the quality of corpus data retrieval and annotation, contrasting with recall, which focuses on the completeness of identified instances. High accuracy indicates that the annotation scheme or retrieval method effectively distinguishes between correct and incorrect classifications.

Definición (ES)

Una medida de la corrección de la anotación de datos, definida como la proporción de resultados verdaderamente positivos entre todas las instancias identificadas por una consulta. Este término es fundamental para evaluar la calidad de la recuperación y anotación de datos en corpus, contrastando con el recall, que se centra en la exhaustividad de las instancias identificadas. Una alta precisión indica que el esquema de anotación o el método de recuperación distingue eficazmente entre clasificaciones correctas e incorrectas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • accuracy — Accuracy is often discussed alongside precision, which measures the proportion of true positives among all positive results returned by a query.
  • recall — Recall contrasts with accuracy by focusing on the completeness of the identified instances rather than the correctness of those identifications.
  • annotation scheme — The effectiveness of an annotation scheme can be evaluated through the accuracy of the annotations it produces.
  • tagger — The accuracy of a tagger is critical in determining how well it assigns correct labels to corpus data.
  • corpus annotation — Accuracy is a key metric in assessing the quality of corpus annotation processes.
  • inter-annotator agreement — High accuracy in annotations can contribute to improved inter-annotator agreement, indicating consistency among different annotators.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "Ideally, the value of both measures should be 1, i.e., our data should include all cases of the phenomenon under investigation (a recall rate of 100 percent) and it should include nothing that is not a case of this phenomenon (a precision of 100 percent)." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)
  • "In these more complex cases, we can, and should, assess the quality of the automatic annotation in the same way in which we would assess the quality of the results returned by a particular query, in terms of precision and recall." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)
  • "Although the degree of accuracy was higher than expected, especially in the earlier subperiods, we can see that the tagger is less precise with earlier texts." (2017_Fanego, T., Rodríguez-Puente, et al._The Corpus of Historical English Law Reports. A resource for analysis the development of English_ICAME)
  • "Most of the tagging errors made by CLAWS correspond to those potential mistakes typical in any kind of text, such as confusion between after, as, before, since and until as prepositions or subordinating conjunctions." (2017_Fanego, T., Rodríguez-Puente, et al._The Corpus of Historical English Law Reports. A resource for analysis the development of English_ICAME)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • "El análisis de errores gana en precisión y posibilidades de generalización si el corpus ha recibido ese tipo de codificación." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)
  • "Los corpus generales permiten, en efecto, extraer datos acerca de las características relevantes de la L2 y hacerlo de forma selectiva en función de los diferentes tipos de texto." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)
  • "El rasgo más habitualmente destacado de los corpus de aprendientes frente a otros es la posibilidad de indicar también, entre los rasgos incorporados en la codificación, el nivel de conocimientos de la L2." (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)
  • "La precisión de la anotación es un aspecto fundamental que se debe considerar al evaluar la calidad de los corpus." (2022_Davies, M., Parodi, G._Constitución de corpus crecientes del español)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "accuracy" is frequently used in the context of data annotation and retrieval, emphasizing the importance of correct classifications in corpus linguistics. Variations in accuracy can arise based on the complexity of the data being annotated and the methods employed, highlighting the need for careful evaluation of annotation schemes and retrieval processes.

El término "precisión" se utiliza con frecuencia en el contexto de la anotación y recuperación de datos, enfatizando la importancia de las clasificaciones correctas en la lingüística de corpus. Las variaciones en la precisión pueden surgir según la complejidad de los datos que se anotan y los métodos empleados, lo que resalta la necesidad de una evaluación cuidadosa de los esquemas de anotación y los procesos de recuperación.

ACTRES

Category / Categoría: Recursos y corpus

Definition (EN)

Research group of the University of León and its bidirectional English-Spanish parallel corpus (P-ACTRES), with texts of different types such as novels, press articles and economic texts.

Definición (ES)

Grupo de investigación de la Universidad de León y su corpus paralelo bidireccional inglés-español (P-ACTRES), con distintos tipos de texto, como novelas, artículos periodísticos y textos de economía.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — P-ACTRES is a parallel corpus.
  • corpus-based translation studies — It is used in contrastive and translation research.
  • bilingual corpus — It is an English-Spanish bilingual corpus.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • The ACTRES parallel corpus: an English– Spanish translation corpus. (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • Con una intención similar, Ramón García (2008) estudia el uso de really como marcador pragmático en P-ACTRES. (2022_Carrió-Pastor, M. L., Alonso-Almeida, F._Corpus paralelos español-inglés)

  • El corpus ACTRES (P-ACTRES 2.0 2018) bidireccional (inglés-español; https://actres. unileon.es) con distintos tipos de texto: novelas, artículos periodísticos, economía, etc. (2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)

  • El corpus ACTRES (P-ACTRES 2.0 2018) bidireccional (inglés-español; https://actres. unileon.es) con distintos tipos de texto: novelas, artículos periodísticos, economía, etc. (2022_Molina Plaza, S._Herramientas, recursos y metodologías de análisis para la traducción mediante corpus lingüísticos del español)

alignment

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

The process of matching corresponding segments in source and target texts, typically at the sentence level, is essential in the creation of parallel corpora. This methodological approach often requires both automatic tools and manual verification to ensure high-quality alignments, as automatic alignment alone may not account for complexities such as sentence merging or splitting. The term is closely related to the concept of multilingual linguistic annotation, which raises questions about comparability across languages.

Definición (ES)

Proceso que establece la correspondencia entre los segmentos equivalentes de un texto original y sus versiones paralelas (sus traducciones), de modo que cada palabra, frase u oración del original pueda identificarse con su expresión correspondiente en las demás versiones. Puede realizarse a distintos niveles (texto, párrafo, oración, frase o palabra), aunque el más habitual es el de la oración, y es fundamental en la creación y explotación de corpus paralelos, por ejemplo para obtener concordancias bilingües o memorias de traducción. Suele combinar herramientas automáticas con revisión manual, ya que la alineación automática no siempre resuelve casos como la fusión o la división de oraciones. También se denomina alineamiento. El término está estrechamente relacionado con la anotación lingüística multilingüe, que plantea interrogantes sobre la comparabilidad entre lenguas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — A parallel corpus is a collection of texts in two languages that are aligned at various levels, making alignment a crucial process for its compilation.
  • annotation — Annotation often accompanies alignment, as it provides additional linguistic information that can enhance the quality of the aligned segments.
  • corpus design — Effective corpus design must consider alignment strategies to ensure that the resulting corpus meets the needs of comparative linguistic analysis.
  • parallel corpus — Translation memory systems utilize alignment techniques to store and retrieve previously translated segments, highlighting the practical applications of alignment in translation.
  • multilingual corpus — A multilingual corpus requires careful alignment across different languages to maintain the integrity and comparability of the data.
  • inter-annotator agreement — Manual verification is often necessary in the alignment process to correct errors that automatic tools may introduce, ensuring the reliability of the aligned texts.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "the performance of the individual alignment tools varies for different types of texts and language pairs and in order to guarantee high quality alignments, a manual verification step is needed." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)
  • "Software tools can be used to align parallel texts automatically at paragraph, sentence and word level." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)
  • "Sentence alignment is not a straightforward task, as translators often merge or split sentences when producing the target text." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)
  • "Such rough alignment yields satisfactory results at the sentence level, especially when it is supported by various statistical methods." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)
  • "The high quality needed for descriptive translation research can only be obtained through manual alignment editing." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • "una alineación incorrecta desvirtuaría los resultados del corpus en los estudios descriptivos realizados con él." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)
  • "la alineación de corpus paralelos es un proceso demandante y laborioso." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)
  • "la alineación cotejada por párrafos permite una alineación más fluida a nivel de oración." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)
  • "la alineación automática de dos documentos que luego puede revisarse de forma manual." (2018_Leiva Rojo, J._Diseño y compilación de corpus paralelos alineados. Dificultades y algunas soluciones)
  • "la alineación es fundamental para optimizar el mapeo entre unidades equivalentes." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "alignment" is primarily used in the context of parallel corpora and translation studies, where it plays a critical role in ensuring the accuracy and reliability of linguistic comparisons across languages. Variations in alignment methods, such as automatic versus manual alignment, reflect ongoing debates about the best practices in corpus linguistics.

El término "alineación" se utiliza principalmente en el contexto de los corpus paralelos y los estudios de traducción, donde desempeña un papel crítico en la garantía de la precisión y fiabilidad de las comparaciones lingüísticas entre lenguas. Las variaciones en los métodos de alineación, como la alineación automática frente a la manual, reflejan debates en curso sobre las mejores prácticas en la lingüística de corpus.

annotated corpus

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A collection of texts that includes additional information beyond the raw text, such as linguistic or metalinguistic features. This additional information can encompass markup, part-of-speech tagging, and semantic tagging, which enhance the corpus's utility for linguistic analysis. The methodological approach to annotation varies, with part-of-speech tagging being the most common form, while other types of annotations may include pragmatic or syntactic information.

Definición (ES)

Un conjunto de textos que incluye información adicional más allá del texto en bruto, como características lingüísticas o metalingüísticas. Esta información adicional puede abarcar etiquetado, etiquetado de partes del discurso y etiquetado semántico, lo que aumenta la utilidad del corpus para el análisis lingüístico. El enfoque metodológico para la anotación varía, siendo el etiquetado de partes del discurso la forma más común, mientras que otros tipos de anotaciones pueden incluir información pragmática o sintáctica.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Annotation is a fundamental component of an annotated corpus, providing the additional linguistic information necessary for analysis.
  • part-of-speech tagging — This is a specific type of annotation commonly found in annotated corpora, essential for grammatical categorization.
  • markup language — Markup languages like XML are often used in the creation of annotated corpora to structure the additional information.
  • corpus design — The design of an annotated corpus involves careful planning to determine the types of annotations that will be included.
  • metadata — Metadata may accompany an annotated corpus, providing contextual information about the data and its collection.
  • semantic annotation — This type of annotation adds layers of meaning to the texts within an annotated corpus, enhancing linguistic analysis.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • A corpus is annotated when it consists of more than the actual words in the document (which is generally known as plain text). (source: 2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)
  • Annotation is a multilayered term that includes (but is not limited to) markup, POS-tagging, and semantic tagging. (source: 2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)
  • Given the predominance of such applications, it comes as no surprise that the most commonly found kind of annotation is part-of-speech tagging. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)
  • Many corpora have begun to feature other kinds of annotation. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)
  • Pragmatically annotated corpora, i.e. corpora that are annotated for speech acts or other pragmatically relevant information, are still relatively rare. (source: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • Se trata de un corpus de la lengua estándar de la variedad del español peninsular, anotado a distintos niveles: morfosintáctico (categoría gramatical y lema), sintáctico (constituyentes y funciones), semántico (sentidos de WordNet, estructura argumental, roles semánticos y entidades) y pragmático (relaciones de correferencia). (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • El CE está parcialmente anotado y lematizado, lo que facilita la investigación lingüística. (fuente: 2022_Molina Plaza, S._Herramientas, recursos y metodologías de análisis para la traducción mediante corpus lingüísticos del español)
  • Entre los corpus anotados de español de libre distribución destacan los corpus ARTHUS asociado a la base de datos ADESSE. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • AnCora constituye una fuente de información para el análisis lingüístico y se ha utilizado profusamente para desarrollar sistemas de análisis automático a diferentes niveles. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • Muchos de ellos son también orientados a tareas, es decir, tratan temas y dominios relativamente limitados, por lo que a menudo no son muy representativos de la interacción hablada general. (fuente: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotated corpus" encompasses a variety of annotation types, reflecting the diverse applications in corpus linguistics. The methodological approaches to annotation are evolving, with increasing attention to pragmatic and semantic dimensions alongside traditional part-of-speech tagging.

El término "corpus anotado" abarca una variedad de tipos de anotación, reflejando las diversas aplicaciones en la lingüística de corpus. Los enfoques metodológicos para la anotación están evolucionando, con una atención creciente a las dimensiones pragmáticas y semánticas junto con el etiquetado tradicional de partes del discurso.

annotation

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A systematic process of enriching linguistic data by adding interpretative information, distinguishing it from markup, which may refer to the physical act of marking text. This practice enhances the corpus's value by allowing for more comprehensive searches and research, as it provides explicit linguistic analysis rather than relying on implicit classifications. The design of annotation systems is often influenced by specific research interests, making it a critical methodological component in corpus linguistics.

Definición (ES)

Un proceso sistemático de enriquecimiento de datos lingüísticos mediante la adición de información interpretativa, que se distingue del marcado, el cual puede referirse al acto físico de marcar un texto. Esta práctica aumenta el valor del corpus al permitir búsquedas y análisis más exhaustivos, ya que proporciona un análisis lingüístico explícito en lugar de depender de clasificaciones implícitas. El diseño de los sistemas de anotación suele estar influenciado por intereses de investigación específicos, lo que lo convierte en un componente metodológico crítico en la lingüística de corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — An annotated corpus is a type of corpus that includes additional interpretative information, enhancing its usability for linguistic research.
  • tagset — The choice of tagset is crucial for annotation, as it determines the categories and labels applied to linguistic data.
  • POS tagging — Part-of-speech tagging is a specific type of annotation that assigns grammatical categories to words in a corpus.
  • metadata — Metadata often accompanies annotations, providing context and additional information about the data being annotated.
  • inter-annotator agreement — This concept is essential for evaluating the reliability of annotations, ensuring that different annotators apply consistent criteria.
  • annotation scheme — An annotation scheme outlines the conventions and guidelines used in the annotation process, influencing the quality and consistency of the annotations.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • Second, the annotation practices need to be documented. This can be done in the form of an annotation manual that outlines the conventions that have been applied in creating a set of annotations and at the same time serves as guidelines for users who intend to implement the annotations themselves on their own corpus data. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)
  • Corpus annotation involves enormous amounts of work. This means that when we decide to use an annotation system or devise one ourselves, we need to make sure that the work is worthwhile, that is, the information we require cannot be extracted in some other way using data that is readily available, such as smarter ways of querying. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)
  • The specific design of annotation systems is codetermined by the specific research interests involved and therefore, we will need to refer to various research projects time and again. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)
  • While the term markup is sometimes used to indicate the physical act of marking specific parts of a text using specific symbols, and, in contrast, annotation may often refer to the interpretative information added, the two may also be used synonymously. (source: 2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)
  • That is, annotation “only means undertaking and making explicit a linguistic analysis”. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)
  • Given the complexity and multi-layeredness of linguistic data, this leads to two main desiderata. One is that, as annotation for more and more subjective characteristics becomes more frequent, it is imperative that annotation provides efficient ways for dealing with ambiguous or otherwise problematic data points. (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L._Linguistic Annotation in or for Corpus Linguistics)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • La anotación de un corpus es un proceso iterativo/cíclico. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • Una vez realizado este proceso en el tiempo que se considere oportuno, es decir, cuando la guía ya no requiere modificaciones y se muestra estable, se pasa a la siguiente fase, la evaluación de la calidad de la anotación. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • Para evaluar la calidad de un corpus anotado el criterio fundamental es la consistencia de los datos anotados, es decir, que todos los anotadores han aplicado el mismo criterio para el mismo problema. (fuente: 2022_Martí, M. A., Taulé, M._Desarrollos tecnológicos de la lingüística de corpus en español)
  • Una gran tasa de acuerdo demuestra que el proceso de anotación es fiable, pero no necesariamente que la anotación es correcta. (fuente: 2022_Moreno Sandoval, A._Etiquetadores morfosintácticos para corpus en español)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation" encompasses various practices in corpus linguistics, often distinguished from markup by its emphasis on interpretative information. Its application is critical for enhancing the usability of linguistic data, and the methodologies surrounding it are continually evolving as new research interests emerge.

El término "anotación" abarca diversas prácticas en la lingüística de corpus, a menudo diferenciándose del marcado por su énfasis en la información interpretativa. Su aplicación es fundamental para aumentar la usabilidad de los datos lingüísticos, y las metodologías que la rodean están en constante evolución a medida que surgen nuevos intereses de investigación.

annotation scheme

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A structured framework for annotating linguistic data, which delineates specific categories and rules for marking entities, relations, and attributes within a text. This methodological tool is essential for ensuring consistency and clarity in the representation of linguistic phenomena, as evidenced by various systems like the ACE Pilot Format and the GNOME coding scheme. Unlike general annotation, an annotation scheme provides a systematic approach to capturing complex linguistic features, such as coreference and anaphoric relations.

Definición (ES)

Marco estructurado para la anotación de datos lingüísticos que delimita categorías específicas y reglas para marcar entidades, relaciones y atributos dentro de un texto. Este instrumento metodológico es esencial para garantizar la consistencia y la claridad en la representación de fenómenos lingüísticos, como evidencian sistemas como el formato ACE Pilot o el esquema de codificación GNOME. A diferencia de la anotación general, un esquema de anotación proporciona un enfoque sistemático para capturar rasgos lingüísticos complejos, tales como la correferencia y las relaciones anafóricas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — An annotation scheme is a specific type of annotation that provides a structured approach to marking linguistic data.
  • annotated corpus — An annotated corpus is created using an annotation scheme, which defines how the data within the corpus is marked and categorized.
  • markup language — An annotation scheme often employs a markup language to encode the annotations within a text, facilitating data processing and analysis.
  • semantic annotation — Many annotation schemes focus on coreference, providing guidelines for marking entities and their references within a text.
  • named entity recognition — An annotation scheme typically includes rules for identifying and categorizing entities mentioned in the text.
  • annotation scheme — Annotation schemes are often accompanied by guidelines that detail the specific rules and categories to be used during the annotation process.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • The annotation system has two basic facets: (1) it captures the identity of referents mentioned by different referring expressions, (2) it captures various aspects of the anaphoric relation. (source: 2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • Anaphoric information in APF is organized around entities: all entities annotated in the document are identified with elements, and each mention of entity e is then recorded as a child element of the element for e. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • Each mention is annotated with the attribute TYPE, with three possible values: NAM for named entities, NOM for NPs with a common noun as head, and PRO for pronouns. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • The ACE guidelines follow a small number of semantic classes considered particularly relevant for information extraction: persons, organizations, locations, geopolitical entities, weapons, and vehicles. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

  • The coding scheme inherits several aspects of the GNOME coding scheme, although with fewer attributes, but adding the ability to annotate discourse deixis. (source: 2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y._Annotated Corpora and Annotation Tools)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation scheme" is widely used in corpus linguistics to refer to structured frameworks that guide the annotation process, ensuring consistency and clarity in data representation. Variations in annotation schemes may arise based on the specific linguistic features being analyzed or the goals of the research.

El término "esquema de anotación" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para referirse a marcos estructurados que guían el proceso de anotación, garantizando consistencia y claridad en la representación de datos. Las variaciones en los esquemas de anotación pueden surgir en función de las características lingüísticas específicas que se analizan o de los objetivos de la investigación.

annotation tools

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

Software applications designed to facilitate the process of adding linguistic labels to textual data, enabling both automated and manual annotation. These tools support various annotation goals, such as parts-of-speech tagging and semantic annotation, and are essential for enhancing the analytical capabilities of corpus linguistics. The corpus indicates a trend towards integrating automated systems with manual annotation processes, highlighting their complementary roles in linguistic research.

Definición (ES)

Aplicaciones informáticas que facilitan el proceso de añadir etiquetas lingüísticas a datos textuales, permitiendo tanto la anotación automática como la manual. Estas herramientas apoyan diversos objetivos de anotación, como el etiquetado de partes del discurso y la anotación semántica, y son esenciales para mejorar las capacidades analíticas de la lingüística de corpus. El corpus indica una tendencia hacia la integración de sistemas automáticos con procesos de anotación manual, destacando sus roles complementarios en la investigación lingüística.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — Annotation tools are used to label and analyze data within a corpus.
  • annotation scheme — Annotation tools often operate based on predefined annotation schemes that dictate how data should be labeled.
  • annotation tools — Many annotation tools provide automated annotation features to streamline the labeling process.
  • annotation tools — Some annotation tools allow for manual annotations, which can complement automated processes.
  • semantic annotation — Annotation tools can be specifically designed for semantic annotation, focusing on the meaning of the text.

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A type of corpus that aims to include equal amounts of text from different sources, such as spoken or written language varieties. The concept is often associated with representativeness, although achieving true balance is considered practically and theoretically challenging, relying heavily on intuition rather than empirical measures. The notion of balance is frequently debated among corpus linguists, with some arguing that it is impossible to create a corpus that meets the criteria of both representativeness and balance.

Definición (ES)

La noción de equilibrio es objeto de debate entre los lingüistas de corpus, con algunos argumentando que es imposible crear un corpus que cumpla con los criterios de representatividad y equilibrio.

BNC

Category / Categoría: Recursos y corpus

Definition (EN)

A large-scale linguistic resource representing a wide range of modern British English, comprising both written and spoken texts. The written component accounts for 90% of the corpus, including diverse text types such as newspapers, academic publications, and fiction, while the spoken part captures informal conversations and various interactional contexts. Initially released in 1995, it serves as a foundational reference corpus for linguistic research and analysis.

Lanzado inicialmente en 1995, sirve como un corpus de referencia fundamental para la investigación y el análisis lingüístico.

Su diseño integral permite una variedad de análisis lingüísticos, aunque su representatividad puede ser cuestionada por la aparición de corpora más grandes basados en la web.

Category / Categoría: Recursos y corpus

Definition (EN)

A widely recognized digital text corpus, this collection consists of 1 million words of American English texts compiled in 1961 by Nelson Francis and Henry Kučera. It serves as a foundational resource in linguistic research, influencing the design of subsequent corpora and methodologies in corpus linguistics. The Brown Corpus is notable for its balanced representation of various text types, contrasting with more specialized corpora that focus on specific genres or registers.

Definición (ES)

El Corpus de Brown es notable por su representación equilibrada de diversos tipos de texto, en contraste con corpora más especializados que se centran en géneros o registros específicos.

  • frequency — The Brown Corpus provides a basis for frequency analysis in linguistic studies, showcasing the distribution of words across different text types.
  • text type — It includes a variety of text types, making it a valuable resource for studying linguistic variation across genres.

chi-squared

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure used to assess the association between categorical variables by comparing observed and expected frequencies. The chi-squared statistic indicates the degree of deviation from independence, with higher values suggesting a stronger association between the variables. This test is commonly employed in corpus linguistics to analyze the significance of variable relationships, contrasting with correlation measures that assess linear relationships.

Definición (ES)

El chi-cuadrado es una medida estadística utilizada para evaluar la asociación entre variables categóricas al comparar frecuencias observadas y esperadas. Este estadístico indica el grado de desviación de la independencia, siendo valores más altos indicativos de una asociación más fuerte entre las variables. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • probability — The chi-squared test relies on probability distributions to determine the significance of the observed associations.
  • statistical significance — The chi-squared value is used to assess whether the association between variables is statistically significant.
  • statistical significance — Unlike correlation, which measures linear relationships, the chi-squared test focuses on categorical data associations.
  • dataset — The chi-squared test is applied to datasets containing categorical variables to analyze their relationships.
  • frequency — This term is central to the chi-squared test, as it compares observed frequencies against expected frequencies.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • R, you do not need to use a χ2 distribution table anymore. > test <- chisq.test(data) > test Pearson's Chi-squared test data: data X-squared = 89.999, df = 6, p-value < 2.2e-16 (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • You test your observed χ2 value for significance by comparing it to the critical χ2 value observed at the intersection of the number of degrees of freedom in your data table and the desired level of significance. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • A chi-squared test compares expected and observed frequencies; greater value of the chi-squared statistic indicates an overall greater difference. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • If you set the level of significance to p = 0.05 (i.e. 5%), then χ2 critical = 12.5916. Your observed χ2 value is larger than χ2 critical with a significance level of p = 0.05. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • The χ2 value is in the test object, under statistic. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • For chi-squared tests we need the observed and expected frequencies. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • It is not recommended to calculate the φ statistic when the matrix is larger than 2×2 because you may get φ > 1, thus going beyond the desired range between 0 and 1. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • The most common measures are: Phi (φ), Pearson’s contingency coefficient, and Cramér’s V. All these measures are derived from χ2. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • You can certainly run chi-squared tests on groups with more than two categories, just like you can run this test on data with more than two groups. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

  • A chi-squared test compares expected and observed frequencies; greater value of the chi-squared statistic indicates an overall greater difference. (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The chi-squared test is a fundamental statistical tool in corpus linguistics, primarily used for analyzing categorical data relationships. Its application is crucial for determining the significance of associations, contrasting it with correlation measures that focus on linear relationships.

El test de chi-cuadrado es una herramienta estadística fundamental en la lingüística de corpus, utilizada principalmente para analizar las relaciones en datos categóricos. Su aplicación es crucial para determinar la significancia de las asociaciones, contrastándolo con las medidas de correlación que se centran en relaciones lineales.

CLAWS

Category / Categoría: Herramientas y software

Definition (EN)

A software tool designed for part-of-speech tagging, which assigns grammatical categories to words in a text. The system is particularly optimized for written language, yet it exhibits limitations when applied to spoken language, as evidenced by its handling of distinct verb forms and pronouns in various contexts. CLAWS operates within a probabilistic framework, allowing for the disambiguation of tags based on contextual usage, which contrasts with simpler tagging methods that do not account for such complexities.

Definición (ES)

CLAWS es una herramienta de software diseñada para el etiquetado de partes del discurso, que asigna categorías gramaticales a las palabras en un texto. El sistema está especialmente optimizado para el lenguaje escrito, aunque presenta limitaciones en su aplicación al lenguaje hablado, lo que se refleja en su tratamiento de determinadas formas verbales y pronombres en distintos contextos. CLAWS opera mediante un marco probabilístico que permite la desambiguación de etiquetas en función del uso contextual, lo que lo diferencia de métodos de etiquetado más simples que no contemplan dicha complejidad.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • tagger — CLAWS functions as a specific type of tagger designed for part-of-speech tagging.
  • POS tagging — The primary function of CLAWS is to perform POS tagging, distinguishing it from other tagging methods.
  • annotation — CLAWS contributes to the annotation process by providing grammatical tags to words in a corpus.
  • corpus annotation — The output of CLAWS is a form of corpus annotation that enhances the usability of linguistic data.
  • grammar — CLAWS relies on grammatical rules to assign appropriate tags to words based on their context.
  • concordance — The tagging performed by CLAWS can facilitate the generation of concordance lines by providing grammatical context.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term CLAWS is primarily associated with part-of-speech tagging in corpus linguistics, emphasizing its role in enhancing the analysis of written texts. Its probabilistic approach to tagging distinguishes it from simpler methods, although its limitations in spoken language contexts are acknowledged.

html:
clustering

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A set of techniques that classify data points into groups based on their similarities, clustering operates without prior information about groupings. This unsupervised method is exploratory, allowing patterns to emerge from the data rather than imposing preconceived notions. Common types include partitioning and hierarchical clustering, which differ in whether the number of groups is specified in advance.

Definición (ES)

Conjunto de técnicas de aprendizaje no supervisado que clasifican los datos en grupos (conglomerados o clusters) según su similitud, sin información previa sobre las agrupaciones. En español se denomina agrupamiento, análisis de conglomerados o análisis de grupos, y también se usa el préstamo clustering. Es un método exploratorio, que permite que surjan patrones en los datos en lugar de imponer nociones preconcebidas. Dos tipos comunes son el agrupamiento por partición y el jerárquico, que difieren en si se especifica o no de antemano el número de grupos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — Clustering techniques often analyze data derived from a corpus to identify patterns.
  • statistical significance — The validity of clusters can be assessed through measures of statistical significance.
  • clustering — A specific type of clustering that produces a dendrogram to illustrate group hierarchies.
  • dataset — Clustering methods typically operate on data frames that contain multiple variables.
  • descriptive statistics — Clustering is a multivariate analysis technique that examines relationships among several variables simultaneously.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "Clustering is done thanks to unsupervised clustering techniques." (source)
  • "The objective of these grouping methods is to create groups with high similarity within the same class and low similarity between different classes." (source)
  • "Two common types of clustering are partitioning and hierarchical clustering." (source)
  • "This type of clustering produces a dendrogram that reflects the hierarchy of the groups." (source)
  • "Clustering methods allow researchers to find structure in multivariate data." (source)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • "Una rama de creciente importancia dentro de los estudios de corpus es el análisis de grupos o clustering." (fuente)
  • "El análisis de grupos comprende de un conjunto de técnicas que clasifican, sin información previa, los puntos de datos en grupos." (fuente)
  • "El análisis de grupos sin supervisión puede ser particularmente útil para un enfoque de 'abajo hacia arriba'." (fuente)
  • "Dos tipos de clustering comunes son la partición y la agrupación jerárquica." (fuente)
  • "Este tipo de clustering produce un diagrama de árbol, conocido como dendrograma." (fuente)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "clustering" is widely used in corpus linguistics to describe methods that explore data without predefined categories, emphasizing its exploratory nature. Variations in usage may arise from different methodological approaches, such as partitioning versus hierarchical clustering, which can affect the interpretation of results.

El término "análisis de grupos" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para describir métodos que exploran datos sin categorías predefinidas, enfatizando su naturaleza exploratoria. Las variaciones en el uso pueden surgir de diferentes enfoques metodológicos, como la partición frente a la agrupación jerárquica, lo que puede afectar la interpretación de los resultados.

COCA

Category / Categoría: Recursos y corpus

Definition (EN)

A large and representative corpus of American English, COCA is designed to reflect everyday language use across various genres, including spoken, fiction, and academic texts. Its balanced structure allows for comprehensive linguistic analysis, making it a preferred choice among researchers for examining contemporary language patterns. The methodological emphasis on representativeness distinguishes COCA from other corpora, such as the British National Corpus (BNC), which focuses on British English.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus extenso y representativo del inglés americano, COCA está diseñado para reflejar el uso del lenguaje cotidiano en diversos géneros, incluyendo textos hablados, de ficción y académicos. Su estructura equilibrada permite un análisis lingüístico integral, convirtiéndolo en una opción preferida entre los investigadores para examinar patrones del lenguaje contemporáneo. El énfasis metodológico en la representatividad distingue a COCA de otros corpus, como el British National Corpus (BNC), que se centra en el inglés británico.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • BNC — COCA serves as a counterpart to the BNC, focusing on American English while the BNC represents British English.
  • corpus — COCA exemplifies a specific type of corpus, known for its size and representativeness in linguistic research.
  • frequency — The analysis of word frequency in COCA provides insights into language usage trends in contemporary American English.
  • corpus design — The methodological framework of COCA is a prime example of corpus design aimed at achieving balance across various text types.
  • general corpus — COCA is categorized as a general corpus due to its wide-ranging representation of everyday language.
  • corpus-based — Research utilizing COCA is often corpus-based, relying on empirical data for linguistic analysis.
  • tagset — The tagging system used in COCA facilitates detailed linguistic analysis, although it has limitations in frequency breakdowns according to tags.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "In COCA, there are six main ‘sections’ labelled ‘tv/movies’, ‘spoken’, ‘fiction’, ‘magazines’, ‘news’, and ‘academic’." (Barth, D., Schnell, S.)
  • "This situation is by no means unique to COCA." (Egbert, J. Biber, D. y Gray, B.)
  • "The main disadvantage of the COCA interface, on the other hand, lies in the fact that it’s not possible to get the frequency breakdown according to tags." (Weisser, M.)
  • "COCA contains texts from different categories in roughly equal proportions." (Barth, D., Schnell, S.)
  • "The research presented here is based on the British National Corpus (BNC) World Edition." (Egbert, J. Biber, D. y Gray, B.)

  • "COCA is representative of North American usage." (Newman & Duncan 2019: 7)

COHA

Category / Categoría: Recursos y corpus

Definition (EN)

A historical corpus of English, this resource contains over 400 million words of text spanning from the 1810s to the 2000s, making it significantly larger than other comparable historical corpora. The corpus is designed to be balanced by genre across decades, which allows for comprehensive linguistic analysis over time. Its extensive size and genre balance facilitate a robust examination of language change and usage patterns.

Definición (ES)

Este corpus histórico del inglés contiene más de 400 millones de palabras de texto desde la década de 1810 hasta la de 2000, lo que lo convierte en un recurso considerablemente más grande que otros corpus históricos comparables. Su diseño equilibrado por géneros a lo largo de las décadas permite un análisis lingüístico exhaustivo a lo largo del tiempo, facilitando el estudio de los cambios y patrones de uso del lenguaje.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — COHA is a specific instance of a corpus, focusing on historical English texts.
  • historical corpus — COHA exemplifies a historical corpus, as it compiles texts from various decades to analyze language evolution.
  • corpus design — The design of COHA emphasizes genre balance, which is a critical aspect of effective corpus design.
  • frequency — The analysis of word frequency within COHA contributes to understanding language trends over time.
  • token — The corpus is composed of tokens, with its size measured in the number of words (tokens) it contains.
  • BNC — While COHA focuses on historical texts, the British National Corpus (BNC) provides a contemporary counterpart for linguistic analysis.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term COHA is specifically used to refer to a large historical corpus, which is distinct from other types of corpora, such as contemporary or learner corpora. Its unique design and extensive size make it a valuable resource for linguistic research focused on historical language use and change.

El término COHA se utiliza específicamente para referirse a un corpus histórico grande, que es distinto de otros tipos de corpus, como los contemporáneos o de aprendientes. Su diseño único y su tamaño extenso lo convierten en un recurso valioso para la investigación lingüística centrada en el uso y cambio del lenguaje a lo largo de la historia.

colligation

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

The concept denotes the statistically significant co-occurrence of specific parts of speech, such as verbs, nouns, and adjectives, within a grammatical framework. Unlike collocation, which focuses on lexical co-occurrences, colligation emphasizes the grammatical relationships and patterns that emerge from these co-occurrences. This term is methodologically relevant in corpus-based studies, as it aids in understanding the structural tendencies of language use.

Definición (ES)

Este concepto se refiere a la co-ocurrencia estadísticamente significativa de partes del habla específicas, como verbos, sustantivos y adjetivos, dentro de un marco gramatical. A diferencia de la colocación, que se centra en las co-ocurrencias léxicas, la coligación enfatiza las relaciones y patrones gramaticales que surgen de estas co-ocurrencias. Este término es relevante metodológicamente en estudios basados en corpus, ya que ayuda a comprender las tendencias estructurales del uso del lenguaje.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • collocation — Colligation is distinct from collocation, which focuses on the co-occurrence of words without a grammatical component.
  • grammar — The concept of colligation is inherently tied to grammar, as it involves the relationships between different parts of speech.
  • corpus-based — The study of colligation is often conducted within corpus-based research methodologies, emphasizing empirical data.
  • association measures — Association measures can be used to quantify the strength of colligational patterns in linguistic data.
  • collocate — Collocates are the specific words that may appear in colligational patterns, highlighting the interaction between lexical and grammatical elements.

  • Colligation is like collocation except that it has a grammatical component. It is therefore the statistically significant co-occurrence of a surface phenomenon (a linguistic form) with a deeper, grammatical phenomenon. (2017_Desagulier, G._Corpus Linguistics and Statistics with R)

  • Para que ese conjunto de textos comience a resultar verdaderamente útil en estudios sobre la adquisición de una segunda lengua es necesario ir añadiendo capas con información referente a las características externas o internas de esos textos. (2022_Rojo, G., Palacios, I._Los corpus de aprendientes de español como L2)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "colligation" is primarily used in the context of grammatical analysis within corpus linguistics, emphasizing the structural relationships between parts of speech. Its distinction from collocation highlights the importance of grammatical frameworks in understanding language patterns.

El término "coligación" se utiliza principalmente en el contexto del análisis gramatical dentro de la lingüística de corpus, enfatizando las relaciones estructurales entre las partes del habla. Su distinción de la colocación resalta la importancia de los marcos gramaticales en la comprensión de los patrones lingüísticos.

collocate

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A word that co-occurs with a node word more frequently than expected within a specified span, indicating a significant association. The identification of collocates can vary among researchers, with some focusing on sequential co-occurrence while others consider structural relationships within grammatical constructions. This term is essential in corpus linguistics for analyzing lexical relations and semantic differences.

Definición (ES)

Una palabra que coocurre con un término nodo con mayor frecuencia de lo esperado dentro de un intervalo específico, lo que indica una asociación significativa. La identificación de colocalizadores puede variar entre investigadores, algunos centrándose en la coocurrencia secuencial y otros considerando relaciones estructurales dentro de construcciones gramaticales. Este término es fundamental en la lingüística de corpus para analizar relaciones léxicas y diferencias semánticas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • collocation — A broader concept that encompasses the specific instances of collocates, focusing on the patterns formed by their co-occurrence.
  • colligation — Refers to the co-occurrence of specific parts of speech, which can be seen as a subset of the broader collocational analysis.
  • association measures — Statistical tools used to quantify the strength of the relationship between collocates and their node words.
  • keyword — A term that may serve as a node word for identifying collocates within a corpus.
  • corpus-based — An approach that relies on empirical data from corpora to study collocational patterns and their significance.

collocation

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A specific type of lexical association, this term denotes the syntagmatic relationship between words, characterized by their co-occurrence within a defined proximity in text. The analysis of collocations is grounded in the principle that the meaning of a target word is influenced by the words surrounding it, as evidenced by the exploration of mutual expectations among collocates. This concept is methodologically significant in corpus linguistics, where it serves as a basis for quantitative research designs assessing word associations.

Definición (ES)

Este término designa una relación léxica específica que se caracteriza por la asociación sintagmática entre palabras, evidenciada por su coocurrencia en una proximidad definida dentro del texto. El análisis de colocaciones se fundamenta en el principio de que el significado de una palabra objetivo se ve influenciado por las palabras que la rodean, lo que se refleja en las expectativas mutuas entre los colocados. Este concepto tiene un estatus metodológico significativo en la lingüística de corpus, sirviendo como base para diseños de investigación cuantitativa que evalúan asociaciones entre palabras.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • collocate — This term refers to the individual words that form a collocation, highlighting the specific lexical items involved in the syntagmatic relationship.
  • phraseology — Collocation is a subset of phraseology, focusing specifically on the predictable patterns of word combinations.
  • concordance — The analysis of collocations often utilizes concordance tools to examine the contexts in which words co-occur.
  • corpus — The study of collocations relies on the analysis of a corpus, which provides the textual data necessary for identifying word associations.
  • frequency — The frequency of collocations can be quantitatively assessed, providing insights into their usage patterns within a corpus.
  • keyword analysis — Collocation analysis can complement keyword analysis by revealing the contextual relationships between frequent terms.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "collocation" is widely used in corpus linguistics to describe specific lexical relationships, often analyzed quantitatively. However, its application may vary across different linguistic traditions, with some scholars advocating for alternative terms that better capture the nuances of these associations.

El término "colocación" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para describir relaciones léxicas específicas, a menudo analizadas de manera cuantitativa. Sin embargo, su aplicación puede variar entre diferentes tradiciones lingüísticas, con algunos académicos abogando por términos alternativos que capturen mejor las sutilezas de estas asociaciones.

collocational strength

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

The measure of the degree to which lexemes co-occur within a specific context, indicating their semantic relationship. Collocational strength is particularly relevant in corpus-based studies, as it highlights distinctions between synonyms by analyzing the relative frequency of co-occurrence compared to non-co-occurrence. This concept is essential for understanding lexical relations and is often assessed using statistical association measures.

Definición (ES)

La fuerza de asociación (o fuerza colocacional) es la medida de la relación entre lexemas basada en su co-ocurrencia en contextos específicos, lo que permite identificar diferencias semánticas. Este concepto es fundamental en los estudios de fraseología y léxico, ya que ayuda a distinguir entre términos que pueden parecer sinónimos a partir de su uso en corpus. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

  • corpus-based — The study of collocational strength is inherently corpus-based, relying on empirical data from linguistic corpora.

El término "fuerza colacional" se utiliza principalmente en el contexto de la lingüística de corpus para analizar relaciones léxicas y se evalúa a menudo mediante diversas medidas estadísticas. comparable corpus

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A collection of texts that are similar in type and content, potentially spanning one or more languages, distinguished from parallel corpora by not requiring direct translations. Comparable corpora are utilized in various linguistic applications, including translation studies, to achieve terminological and stylistic cohesion. They serve as valuable resources for researchers aiming to analyze language use across different contexts and genres.

Definición (ES)

Colección de textos que son similares en tipo y contenido, que pueden abarcar una o más lenguas, y que se diferencian de los corpus paralelos al no requerir traducciones directas. Los corpus comparables se utilizan en diversas aplicaciones lingüísticas, incluyendo los estudios de traducción, para lograr cohesión terminológica y estilística. Son recursos valiosos para investigadores que buscan analizar el uso del lenguaje en diferentes contextos y géneros.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — A type of corpus that contains original texts in one language along with their translations in another language, contrasting with comparable corpora which do not require direct translations.
  • reference corpus — A broader category that may include comparable corpora as part of its design to provide comprehensive linguistic information.
  • corpus compilation — The process that includes the creation of comparable corpora, emphasizing the methodological aspects of gathering similar texts.
  • multilingual corpus — A category that can encompass comparable corpora, particularly when they involve texts from multiple languages.
  • corpus design — The methodological framework that guides the creation of comparable corpora, focusing on the selection and organization of texts.
  • corpus annotation — A process that may be applied to comparable corpora to enhance their usability for linguistic analysis.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "comparable corpus" has gained prominence in recent years, particularly in the context of translation studies and cross-linguistic research. Its usage reflects a methodological approach that emphasizes the analysis of similar texts rather than direct translations, which distinguishes it from parallel corpora.

Su uso refleja un enfoque metodológico que enfatiza el análisis de textos similares en lugar de traducciones directas, lo que lo distingue de los corpus paralelos.

computational corpus linguistics

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

Branch of corpus linguistics that uses computational tools, both hardware and software, to build and exploit corpora. It is distinguished from corpus-based computational linguistics, which uses the corpora so built to study language computationally.

Definición (ES)

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus-based computational linguistics — The two labels are explicitly contrasted in the Spanish subcorpus.
  • corpus linguistics — It is a branch of corpus linguistics.
  • computational linguistics — It borrows tools and methods from computational linguistics.
  • corpus compilation — Its main concern is the construction of corpora.

computational linguistics

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A branch of linguistics that focuses on the development of algorithms and computational models for processing and analyzing human language. This field intersects with natural language processing and corpus linguistics, emphasizing the use of computational tools to enhance linguistic research and applications. The methodological advancements in computational linguistics have significantly influenced the empirical study of language, enabling more accurate analyses of linguistic phenomena.

Definición (ES)

Una rama de la lingüística que se centra en el desarrollo de algoritmos y modelos computacionales para el procesamiento y análisis del lenguaje humano. Este campo se entrelaza con el procesamiento del lenguaje natural y la lingüística de corpus, destacando el uso de herramientas computacionales para mejorar la investigación y aplicaciones lingüísticas. Los avances metodológicos en la lingüística computacional han influido significativamente en el estudio empírico del lenguaje, permitiendo análisis más precisos de los fenómenos lingüísticos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus linguistics — Computational linguistics often utilizes methods and findings from corpus linguistics to inform its algorithms and models.
  • natural language processing — This term is closely related as computational linguistics provides the theoretical foundation for the development of natural language processing technologies.
  • corpus-based — Many computational linguistics applications are corpus-based, relying on large datasets of authentic language use for training models.
  • annotation — Annotation is a crucial process in computational linguistics, as it involves labeling data for machine learning and linguistic analysis.
  • statistical significance — Statistical significance is often a key consideration in computational linguistics when evaluating the performance of algorithms and models.
  • dataset — A data set serves as the foundational element in computational linguistics, providing the necessary input for analysis and model training.

concordance

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A method for retrieving and displaying instances of a specific word or phrase within a text, highlighting its surrounding context. This technique allows researchers to analyze patterns of usage and semantic relationships, often employing software tools that facilitate the extraction of relevant data from corpora. The methodological significance of concordance is underscored by its application in both qualitative and quantitative linguistic studies.

Definición (ES)

Método para recuperar y mostrar instancias de una palabra o frase específica dentro de un texto, resaltando su contexto circundante. Esta técnica permite a los investigadores analizar patrones de uso y relaciones semánticas, utilizando a menudo herramientas informáticas que facilitan la extracción de datos relevantes de los corpus. La importancia metodológica de la concordancia se destaca por su aplicación en estudios lingüísticos tanto cualitativos como cuantitativos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — A concordance is derived from a corpus, which serves as the foundational dataset for analysis.
  • query — The process of generating a concordance often involves formulating specific queries to extract relevant text segments.
  • frequency — Concordance analysis can reveal the frequency of specific terms or phrases within a corpus, contributing to lexical studies.
  • collocation — The examination of concordance lines can help identify collocations, or words that frequently occur together in a given context.
  • annotation — Annotated corpora can enhance concordance results by providing additional linguistic information about the words being analyzed.
  • keyword — A keyword can serve as the focal point for generating a concordance, allowing researchers to explore its usage across different texts.

confidence interval

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A statistical range that indicates the degree of uncertainty around a sample mean, allowing researchers to estimate the true population mean with a specified level of confidence. The width of the confidence interval is inversely related to the sample size, meaning larger samples yield more precise estimates. This concept is essential for understanding the tolerable error in estimating population parameters based on sample statistics.

Definición (ES)

Un rango estadístico que indica el grado de incertidumbre alrededor de una media muestral, permitiendo a los investigadores estimar la verdadera media poblacional con un nivel de confianza especificado. El ancho del intervalo de confianza está inversamente relacionado con el tamaño de la muestra, lo que significa que muestras más grandes producen estimaciones más precisas. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • sample size — The required number of observations needed to achieve a desired confidence interval, with larger sample sizes leading to narrower intervals.
  • standard deviation — A measure of dispersion that influences the width of the confidence interval; higher standard deviations result in wider intervals.
  • population — The entire group from which a sample is drawn, with the confidence interval providing an estimate of a parameter for this larger group.
  • mean score — The average value calculated from a sample, which the confidence interval seeks to estimate within a range of error.
  • statistical significance — A concept that relates to the likelihood that a result is not due to chance, often assessed within the context of confidence intervals.

  • The confidence interval is the window within which we can be 95% certain that the true population mean falls. (source)

  • All else being equal, it will require a larger sample to precisely analyze a linguistic feature that has a large standard deviation. (source)

  • Thus, the confidence interval relates to the degree of precision that we hope to achieve. (source)

  • A survey of the literature revealed some studies that use a form of the word “estimate” to refer to the relationship between a corpus sample and a target population. (source)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The concept of confidence interval is crucial in statistical analysis, particularly in the context of estimating population parameters from sample data. Variations in its application may arise based on the chosen confidence level and the nature of the data being analyzed.

El concepto de intervalo de confianza es crucial en el análisis estadístico, especialmente en el contexto de la estimación de parámetros poblacionales a partir de datos muestrales. Las variaciones en su aplicación pueden surgir en función del nivel de confianza elegido y la naturaleza de los datos analizados.

content words

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

Lexical items that convey significant semantic meaning, distinguishing them from function words, which primarily serve grammatical purposes. Content words include proper nouns, common nouns, adjectives, and verbs, and are essential for conveying the core information of a text. Their identification is crucial in frequency analyses to explore semantically relevant vocabulary, as they significantly contribute to the overall meaning of language data.

Definición (ES)

Las palabras que aportan un significado semántico significativo, diferenciándose de las palabras funcionales, que cumplen principalmente funciones gramaticales. Las palabras de contenido incluyen nombres propios, sustantivos comunes, adjetivos y verbos, y son esenciales para transmitir la información central de un texto. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • function word — Content words are contrasted with function words, which serve grammatical roles rather than conveying significant meaning.
  • frequency — The analysis of content words is crucial in frequency studies to identify semantically relevant vocabulary in a corpus.
  • parts of speech — Content words are a specific category within the broader classification of parts of speech, which includes nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.
  • keyword — Content words often serve as keywords in texts, representing the main topics or themes.
  • collocation — The study of collocations often focuses on content words, as they form the core of meaningful phrases.
  • corpus-based — The identification and analysis of content words are fundamental in corpus-based linguistic research.

corpus

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A large, principled sample of texts designed to represent a target domain of language use. This foundational concept in corpus linguistics serves as the basis for empirical research, allowing for generalizations about linguistic patterns within a specific context. The methodological status of a corpus is critical, as it influences the representativeness and validity of linguistic analyses derived from it.

Definición (ES)

Conjunto amplio y sistemático de textos que busca representar un dominio específico del uso del lenguaje. Este concepto fundamental en la lingüística de corpus es esencial para la investigación empírica, ya que permite realizar generalizaciones sobre patrones lingüísticos en contextos determinados. La calidad metodológica de un corpus es crucial, ya que afecta la representatividad y validez de los análisis lingüísticos que se derivan de él.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus linguistics — Corpus is the foundational concept upon which corpus linguistics is built, enabling the study of language through large text samples.
  • representativeness — The representativeness of a corpus directly impacts the validity of linguistic generalizations made from it.
  • sample — A corpus can be viewed as a specific type of sample that is systematically compiled to reflect a broader linguistic population.
  • corpus design — The process of corpus design is essential for ensuring that the corpus accurately represents the intended linguistic domain.
  • general corpus — A general corpus is a subtype of corpus that encompasses a wide range of texts, contrasting with specialized corpora that focus on specific language varieties.
  • annotated corpus — An annotated corpus includes additional information about the texts, enhancing the analytical potential of the corpus.
  • corpus compilation — The process of corpus compilation involves the systematic gathering and organization of texts to create a corpus.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • A corpus is a large, principled sample of texts designed to represent a target domain of language use. (2022_Egbert J. Biber D. y Gray B.)
  • Most corpus research aims to generalize results from a corpus to the target domain. (2022_Egbert J. Biber D. y Gray B.)
  • Corpus representativeness is the extent to which a corpus permits accurate and meaningful generalizations about linguistic patterns that are typical in a domain. (2022_Egbert J. Biber D. y Gray B.)
  • The goal is to refer to some of the big digital corpora available today with a focus on the patterns of their formation, the type of content included in them, and the way these corpora are being used in various linguistic works. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)
  • Following these scholars, within a span of six decades, a large number of text and speech corpora were developed in various parts of the world. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

Fuentes del corpus (ES) / Corpus sources (ES)

  • Corpus constituido por textos pertenecientes a una única lengua. (2021_Rojo, G.)
  • Se trata de un corpus de una variedad específica de lengua que incluye exclusivamente materiales pertenecientes a la mencionada variedad. (2023_Hernández García, V.)
  • Un corpus de propósito general, diseñado para que pueda ser utilizado en estudios de tipos muy diferentes. (2021_Rojo, G.)
  • Corpus concebido y presentado como una muestra de una lengua, una variedad lingüística, una corriente literaria, etc. (2021_Rojo, G.)
  • La construcción de un corpus hoy en día puede llevarse a cabo a través de diversas investigaciones sobre el lenguaje con corpus ya existentes. (2018_Bernal Chávez, J. A. . Hincapié Moreno, D. A.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "corpus" is foundational in the field of corpus linguistics, with its definition evolving alongside advancements in digital technology and linguistic research methodologies. Variations in corpus types, such as monolingual, multilingual, and specialized corpora, reflect the diverse applications and contexts in which corpora are utilized.

El término "corpus" es fundamental en el campo de la lingüística de corpus, y su definición ha evolucionado junto con los avances en tecnología digital y metodologías de investigación lingüística. Las variaciones en los tipos de corpus, como los monolingües, multilingües y especializados, reflejan las diversas aplicaciones y contextos en los que se utilizan los corpus.

corpus compilation

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

The process of gathering and organizing a set of texts to create a representative sample for linguistic analysis. This involves making decisions about corpus design, structure, and the publication of the corpus, which is essential for ensuring accessibility and usability for researchers. The methodological considerations in corpus compilation are crucial for achieving representativeness and facilitating meaningful generalizations about language use.

Definición (ES)

El proceso de reunir y organizar un conjunto de textos con el fin de crear una muestra representativa para el análisis lingüístico. Esto implica tomar decisiones sobre el diseño y la estructura del corpus, así como sobre su publicación, lo cual es esencial para garantizar la accesibilidad y la usabilidad para los investigadores. Las consideraciones metodológicas en la compilación de corpus son cruciales para lograr la representatividad y facilitar generalizaciones significativas sobre el uso del lenguaje.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus design — Corpus compilation is a critical aspect of corpus design, as it involves the selection and organization of texts to meet specific research goals.
  • representativeness — The effectiveness of corpus compilation is often evaluated based on the representativeness of the texts included in the corpus.
  • metadata — Proper corpus compilation includes the integration of metadata to provide context and facilitate the understanding of the corpus by users.
  • corpus compilation — The final step in corpus compilation is corpus publication, which ensures that the compiled data is accessible to researchers and practitioners.
  • corpus annotation — Corpus compilation may involve annotation processes to enhance the usability and analytical potential of the texts gathered.
  • sample — A well-compiled corpus serves as a sample that reflects the linguistic features of a larger population.

Fuentes del corpus (EN) / Corpus sources (EN)

  • "The final step in corpus compilation is publication." (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)
  • "Considerations of corpus design will also apply to compilations of small, focused research corpora." (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S._Understanding Corpus Linguistics)
  • "Corpus representativeness is the extent to which a corpus permits accurate and meaningful generalizations about linguistic patterns." (2022_Egbert_ J. Biber_ D. y Gray_ B._Designing and Evaluating Language Corpora)
