  • phraseology — Semantic prosody is a key aspect of phraseology, influencing the meaning of multi-word expressions.

SGML

Category / Categoría: Estándares y formatos técnicos

Definition (EN)

A markup format that requires a Document Type Definition (DTD) to specify its structure, enabling serious processing of annotated data. SGML is characterized by its complexity and the necessity for strict adherence to its coding standards, which can lead to errors if not properly managed. Compared to HTML and XML, SGML is less flexible and not widely supported by standard browser software, making it more challenging for corpus annotation tasks.

Definición (ES)

Un formato de marcado que requiere una Definición de Tipo de Documento (DTD) para especificar su estructura, lo que permite un procesamiento serio de los datos anotados. SGML se caracteriza por su complejidad y la necesidad de cumplir estrictamente con sus estándares de codificación, lo que puede dar lugar a errores si no se gestiona adecuadamente. En comparación con HTML y XML, SGML es menos flexible y no está ampliamente soportado por software de navegador estándar, lo que lo hace más desafiante para las tareas de anotación de corpus.

standard deviation

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure of dispersion, this value quantifies the extent to which individual data points differ from the mean of a dataset. It is calculated as the square root of the variance, which itself is derived from the average of the squared differences between each data point and the mean. The standard deviation is widely utilized in corpus linguistics to assess variability in frequency distributions, although it may not be ideal for skewed data distributions.

Definición (ES)

Medida estadística de la dispersión, este valor cuantifica el grado en que los puntos de datos individuales difieren de la media de un conjunto de datos. Se calcula como la raíz cuadrada de la varianza, que a su vez se deriva del promedio de las diferencias al cuadrado entre cada punto de datos y la media. La desviación estándar se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para evaluar la variabilidad en las distribuciones de frecuencia, aunque puede no ser ideal para distribuciones de datos sesgadas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • sample size — The calculation of standard deviation is influenced by sample size, as a larger sample can lead to a more accurate estimate of variability.
  • confidence interval — The standard deviation plays a crucial role in determining the width of confidence intervals in statistical analyses.
  • descriptive statistics — Standard deviation is a key component of descriptive statistics, summarizing the spread of data points in a dataset.
  • probability — Understanding standard deviation is essential for interpreting probabilities associated with normal distributions.

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A lexical item characterized by its high frequency and low semantic content, often excluded from analyses to enhance the clarity of keyword identification. Su uso metodológico es habitual en la lingüística de corpus, donde se filtran para mejorar la calidad del modelado de temas y el análisis de palabras clave. Se distinguen de las palabras de contenido, que poseen significado referencial y resultan fundamentales para comprender el tema del texto.

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure used to determine the significance of differences between groups, calculated by comparing the mean of a sample to a known value while accounting for variability. The t-score is particularly relevant in hypothesis testing and is often employed in conjunction with other statistical measures to assess the strength of collocations and their significance in linguistic analysis. This term is methodologically grounded in corpus linguistics, where it aids in identifying significant patterns in language use.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística utilizada para determinar la significación de las diferencias entre grupos, calculada al comparar la media de una muestra con un valor conocido, teniendo en cuenta la variabilidad. La puntuación t es especialmente relevante en las pruebas de hipótesis y se emplea a menudo junto con otras medidas estadísticas para evaluar la fuerza de las colocaciones y su significación en el análisis lingüístico.

  • mean score — The t-score is derived from the mean score of a sample compared to a known population mean.

A category of written or spoken material characterized by specific linguistic features and intended for particular communicative purposes. Text types can vary significantly, as seen in the distinction between general text corpora and specialized categories such as 'Email Corpus' or 'Speech Corpus', which are designed for targeted analysis. The methodological implications of identifying text types are crucial for corpus design, as they influence the representativeness and applicability of the corpus data.

token

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A basic unit of text that is counted in linguistic analysis, representing each occurrence of a word form regardless of its frequency. Tokens are distinguished from types, which refer to unique word forms in a text, highlighting the difference between total occurrences and distinct words. The methodology of counting tokens can vary across corpora, as seen in the treatment of clitic forms in different datasets.

Definición (ES)

Unidad básica de texto que se cuenta en el análisis lingüístico, representando cada ocurrencia de una forma léxica sin importar su frecuencia. Los tokens se diferencian de los types, que se refieren a las formas de palabras únicas en un texto, destacando la diferencia entre las ocurrencias totales y las palabras distintas. La metodología para contar tokens puede variar entre diferentes corpus, como se observa en el tratamiento de las formas clíticas en distintos conjuntos de datos.

tokenisation

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

The process of segmenting text into individual units, known as tokens, which can include words, phrases, or symbols. This methodological step is crucial in corpus linguistics as it influences the quality of data analysis, particularly in relation to the accuracy of frequency counts and statistical measures. Tokenisation is often contrasted with the treatment of punctuation and numbers, which can skew results if not properly defined.

Definición (ES)

La tokenización es el proceso de segmentar un texto en unidades individuales, conocidas como tokens, que pueden incluir palabras, frases o símbolos. Este paso metodológico es fundamental en la lingüística de corpus, ya que influye en la calidad del análisis de datos, especialmente en relación con la precisión de los conteos de frecuencia y las medidas estadísticas. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

  • frequency — The accuracy of frequency counts is directly affected by the method of tokenisation employed in the corpus.
  • corpus design — Effective corpus design requires careful consideration of tokenisation strategies to ensure data quality.
  • concordance — Tokenisation is essential for generating concordances, as it determines how text is segmented for analysis.
  • raw frequency — Raw frequency counts depend on the correct identification of tokens during the tokenisation process.

Category / Categoría: Metodología y diseño

Definition (EN)

A specialized collection of texts used to develop and evaluate language processing models, characterized by its systematic selection of data that reflects the linguistic features relevant to the intended application. treebank

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento lingüístico

Definition (EN)

A structured corpus that contains syntactically analyzed sequences, allowing for the retrieval of sentences that meet specific structural conditions. Treebanks serve as essential resources in natural language processing, particularly for training parsers, and are characterized by their use of tree structures to represent grammatical relationships. Notably, the Penn Treebank is a widely recognized example, illustrating the methodological significance of treebank annotations in linguistic research.

Definición (ES)

Los corpus anotados sintácticamente (treebanks) son recursos esenciales en el procesamiento del lenguaje natural, especialmente para el entrenamiento de analizadores, y se caracterizan por el uso de estructuras arbóreas para representar relaciones gramaticales. Un ejemplo ampliamente reconocido es el RST Spanish Treebank, que ilustra la importancia metodológica de las anotaciones en los bancos de árboles en la investigación lingüística.

  • dependency parsing — Some treebanks are designed specifically for dependency parsing, contrasting with phrase structure treebanks.
  • annotated corpus — A treebank is a form of annotated corpus that provides detailed syntactic information.
  • parsing — The primary focus of a treebank is the syntactic structure of sentences, making it a key resource for syntax studies.

type-token ratio

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure in corpus linguistics that expresses the diversity of vocabulary within a sample, calculated by dividing the number of unique types by the total number of tokens. This ratio indicates the proportion of distinct words relative to the total word count, reflecting lexical richness and variation in the text. Methodologically, it is essential for comparing linguistic phenomena across different samples, as it accounts for sample size variability.

Definición (ES)

Medida cuantitativa en lingüística de corpus que expresa la diversidad léxica de una muestra, calculada dividiendo el número de tipos únicos entre el total de tokens. Este índice refleja la proporción de palabras distintas en relación con el recuento total de palabras, dando cuenta de la riqueza léxica y la variación textual. Metodológicamente, resulta esencial para comparar fenómenos lingüísticos entre distintas muestras, ya que contempla la variabilidad en el tamaño de la muestra.

  • frequency — Frequency refers to the number of times a word appears, which directly affects the total token count used in the type-token ratio calculation.
  • corpus — A corpus provides the data necessary for calculating the type-token ratio, as it contains the tokens and types being analyzed.
  • sample — A sample is a subset of a corpus from which the type-token ratio is derived, highlighting the importance of sample size in this measurement.
  • normalized frequency — Normalized frequency adjusts raw frequency counts, which can be relevant when discussing type-token ratios across different corpora or text lengths.

Category / Categoría: Estándares y formatos técnicos

Definition (EN)

A character encoding that uses a variable number of bytes to represent characters, allowing for the inclusion of a vast array of symbols from multiple languages. Its adoption is increasingly becoming the standard for text processing in various computational applications.

Su adopción se está convirtiendo en el estándar para el procesamiento de texto en diversas aplicaciones computacionales.

  • metadata — UTF-8 is a type of metadata that specifies how text data is encoded, impacting data retrieval and processing.

word frequency

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure indicating how often specific word forms appear within a given text or corpus. This metric is essential for generating frequency lists, which can be sorted to reveal patterns in language use, such as identifying the most common or least common words. The methodology for calculating word frequency often involves tokenization and normalization processes to ensure accuracy across different corpora.

Definición (ES)

Una medida cuantitativa que indica con qué frecuencia aparecen formas específicas de palabras dentro de un texto o corpus determinado. Este concepto es fundamental para generar listas de frecuencia, que pueden ordenarse para revelar patrones en el uso del lenguaje, como la identificación de las palabras más comunes o menos comunes. La metodología para calcular la frecuencia de palabras a menudo implica procesos de segmentación y normalización para garantizar la precisión en diferentes corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • frequency list — A frequency list is a compilation of word types along with their respective frequencies, derived from the analysis of word frequency.
  • token — A token represents each instance of a word form in a text, which is essential for calculating word frequency.
  • raw frequency — Raw frequency refers to the total count of occurrences of a word form, which is a foundational component in determining word frequency.
  • normalized frequency — Normalized frequency adjusts raw frequency based on the size of the corpus, providing a more meaningful comparison of word frequency across different texts.
  • stopword — Stopwords are often excluded from frequency counts, as they typically contribute little to the semantic content of a text, contrasting with the focus on significant word frequency.
  • lemma — A lemma is the base form of a word, and its frequency can be analyzed to understand the usage of different inflected forms within a corpus.

XML

Category / Categoría: Estándares y formatos técnicos

Definition (EN)

A markup language that allows users to define their own tags, facilitating the creation of structured documents. XML enhances the separation of content from presentation, enabling better organization and retrieval of information within corpora. It is often contrasted with HTML, which is more rigid in its predefined tags and structure.

z-score

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure that describes a value's relation to the mean of a group of values, expressed in terms of standard deviations. This metric is essential in quantitative linguistics for assessing the significance of linguistic features within a corpus. Unlike raw scores, z-scores standardize data, allowing for comparisons across different datasets or distributions.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística que describe la relación de un valor con la media de un grupo de valores, expresada en términos de desviaciones estándar. Este concepto es fundamental en la lingüística cuantitativa para evaluar la significación de características lingüísticas dentro de un corpus. Término no documentado en el subcorpus español.

Zipf's law

Category / Categoría: Estadística y léxico

Definition (EN)

Empirical law according to which the frequency of a word in a text or corpus is inversely proportional to its rank in the frequency list, so that a few words are very frequent and most words are rare. It explains why large corpora are needed to observe low-frequency items.

Definición (ES)

Explica por qué hacen falta corpus grandes para observar las unidades poco frecuentes.
